moments.title: AI in compensation
moments.speaker: Q Hamirani
moments.why: Describes building an AI model for real-time compensation using Radford data.

moments.title: AI as capacity unlock
moments.speaker: Q Hamirani
moments.why: Frames AI as freeing up humans for higher-value work, not just replacing jobs.

moments.title: Drivers for HRIS change
moments.speaker: Q Hamirani
moments.why: Explains hypergrowth and fragmented systems as key reasons for adopting Darwinbox.

moments.title: Human-in-the-loop for AI decisions
moments.speaker: Q Hamirani
moments.why: Stresses need for checkpoints when AI makes decisions in HR processes.

moments.title: AI as teammate, not replacement
moments.speaker: Q Hamirani
moments.why: Positions AI as a tool to augment human judgment in change management and comms.

moments.title: Agility and real-time insights
moments.speaker: Q Hamirani
moments.why: Emphasizes need for agility in fast-changing tech and global environment.

moments.title: Controlled AI experimentation
moments.speaker: Q Hamirani
moments.why: Advocates testing AI in safe, internal environments before scaling.

moments.title: Pace of AI change and risk
moments.speaker: Q Hamirani
moments.why: Notes fear comes from speed of AI tool evolution and unvetted options.

insights.insight: Global scalability and local compliance are non-negotiable when choosing HR tech for multinational teams.
insights.speaker: Q Hamirani
insights.so_what: HR leaders must ensure tools handle both global consistency and local legal nuances like state-specific time tracking.

insights.insight: Embedded analytics in HRIS eliminate the need for a dedicated people analytics team to start gaining insights.
insights.speaker: Q Hamirani
insights.so_what: Teams can leverage built-in storyboards and reporting to drive decisions without heavy upfront investment in analytics headcount.

insights.insight: AI in HR should be evaluated by whether it enables 'doing more with less' without sacrificing human judgment in sensitive areas.
insights.speaker: Q Hamirani
insights.so_what: Success isn't just automation—it's augmenting HR capacity while preserving empathy and context in people decisions.

insights.insight: Guardrails for AI in HR must include controlled experimentation, data privacy, and human validation of outputs to prevent hallucination and misuse.
insights.speaker: Q Hamirani
insights.so_what: Trust but verify: pilot AI in sandbox environments, validate outputs with business context, and restrict access to sensitive models.

insights.insight: The most valuable HR uses of AI augment—rather than replace—human skills like coaching, performance conversations, and change management.
insights.speaker: Q Hamirani
insights.so_what: Leaders should invest in AI that frees time for high-touch, relational work that machines cannot replicate.

quotes.quote: we have experienced tremendous hyper growth in the last year or two
quotes.speaker: Q Hamirani

quotes.quote: can it meet the needs of our global employee base?
quotes.speaker: Q Hamirani

quotes.quote: we've been able to train our own models to give us almost real-time compensation based on a job description
quotes.speaker: Q Hamirani

quotes.quote: it's not a one and done thing
quotes.speaker: Q Hamirani

quotes.quote: you have to figure out where you want to have kind of human in the loop checkpoints
quotes.speaker: Q Hamirani

quotes.quote: I don't view AI specifically as a new thing that's taking away people's jobs
quotes.speaker: Q Hamirani

quotes.quote: it's taken away a small subset of jobs and unlocked capacity from those individuals to do things that they were not able to do before
quotes.speaker: Q Hamirani

quotes.quote: the true human connection, I don't think, I'm a strong believer, cannot be replaced in work or even in life truly with AI
quotes.speaker: Q Hamirani
